title: La Minerva vs Bulgari Rome: Warm Palazzo or Modern Scene? (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Orient Express La Minerva vs Bulgari Hotel Roma, compared by a travel advisor who stayed at La Minerva and visited the Bulgari in October 2026: mood, room size, dining, gym, neighborhood, and who each one suits.

hero.alt: A suite living room at Orient Express La Minerva, Rome

sub: Both are for travelers who want energy. One gets it from a warm team in a real neighborhood by the Pantheon; the other from marble, mosaics and more bars than I could count. Here is how I would choose.
stamp: Stayed at La Minerva · Visited the Bulgari · October 2026

choose.lead: The warmest shared spaces and the friendliest team I found in Rome, by the Pantheon, in a hotel where I felt I could be myself.

choose.h3: If you want space and a polished scene
choose.lead: Very large base rooms, marble and mosaics, a rooftop bar, a trattoria with €18 pastas and the biggest gym I saw in Rome.

band.h2: Do you want the buzz of a neighborhood, or the buzz of a scene?
paras: La Minerva and the Bulgari both suit travelers who want energy. They get it in different ways.
At La Minerva, it is the people. The team is the warmest I met in Rome, the bar and lobby downstairs have a real buzz, and you step out into a real Roman neighborhood by the Pantheon.

At the Bulgari, it is the hotel itself: very modern and lively, with base rooms the size of junior suites and more places to eat and drink than I could count. If a big room matters, pick the Bulgari. If personality and a neighborhood matter more, pick La Minerva.

guide.alt: A Bulgari Hotel Roma bedroom with a tall upholstered headboard and round brass reading lights
paras: The base rooms at the Bulgari are what other hotels would call deluxe rooms or even junior suites, so the entry rate already buys real space. Because the base category is so generous, you often do not need to upgrade.
At La Minerva, the highlight of my stay was the shared spaces: the restaurant upstairs, the bar downstairs and the lobby. If a big room is high on your list, the Bulgari is the one to book.

guide.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma rooftop at sunset, a brick walkway under green arches lined with lounge seating
paras: Honestly, I am not even sure how many places there are to eat and drink at the Bulgari. There is a beautiful rooftop bar and pizza restaurant, another bar below it, and a classic Roman trattoria downstairs with affordable dishes like €18 pastas. I loved that.
At La Minerva, the rooftop restaurant is where I would spend the evening, looking over the domes of the centro storico, and the bar downstairs is a shared space you actually want to sit in.

guide.alt: The lobby lounge at Orient Express La Minerva
paras: La Minerva is relaxed. I felt like I could be myself there, and I shared a great laugh with the woman who checked me in.
The Bulgari is lively too, almost like an EDITION but much more sophisticated, with lots of marble and incredible mosaics in the bathrooms. It is spectacular.

guide.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma gym, with Technogym racks, benches and plates against warm wood paneling
paras: The Bulgari has the biggest gym I saw in Rome, massive and with serious equipment, plus a spa.

At La Minerva, the extras come through me: daily breakfast for two, a $100 USD hotel credit, an upgrade on arrival and a VIP welcome, and Signature Suite bookings can include a 50-minute massage for two. It is also where I put clients before La Dolce Vita.

faq.q: Which is better, La Minerva or the Bulgari?
faq.a: It depends on the trip. La Minerva for warmth, personality and a real neighborhood by the Pantheon. The Bulgari for space, a lively scene and great dining without leaving the hotel.
The Bulgari. Its base rooms are the size of junior suites at a lot of hotels.

faq.q: Which is better for younger travelers?
faq.a: La Minerva, for the warmest shared spaces and the friendliest team I met in Rome. The Bulgari is lively but more polished.
The Bulgari, with the biggest gym I saw in Rome, plus a spa.

The Bulgari has more places to eat and drink than I could count, including a trattoria with €18 pastas. At La Minerva, the rooftop restaurant is where I would spend the evening, and you are by the Pantheon with Rome on your doorstep.
